svg.text: Editor crashes — cause, fix, and prevention
2026-09-18 · two fatal classes found in the logs · one fixed and guarded, one scripted but not yet run
Crash 1 — out of memory, 2026-09-18 14:34
Re-importing the Guidemen source with bake_meshes = True. The log shows the script stack and the numbers:
Script Stack: /Script/InterchangeEngine.InterchangeManager.ImportAsset
Ran out of memory allocating 1485644460 (1416.8 MiB) bytes
Last error msg: The paging file is too small for this operation to complete
PeakUsedVirtual 135348469760 (126.05 GiB) AvailableVirtual 1.15 GiB
Why: the source is shared-mesh instanced — 18,823 nodes over 48 geometries.
Baking writes every node out as its own mesh. Preflight measured what that costs:
Guidemen_GuideGate_UE5_100M_Instanced 18,823 nodes / 48 geoms -> ~148 GB baked
GreatSouthGate_Zhengnanmen_UE5_HighPoly 2,449 nodes / 16 geoms -> ~2791 GB baked
The fix — two new tools and six guards
Scripts/ImportPreflight.py
Audits every GLB in the project from its JSON chunk alone — no geometry decode — and
returns SAFE / BAKE-FORBIDDEN / LARGE / REFUSE with the projected gigabytes. Also reports
the machine's commit headroom, because the failure mode is the commit limit.
5 GLBs BAKE-FORBIDDEN · 6 LARGE · everything else SAFE
A hard guard in all six bake-on-import scripts
Self-contained, inlined before each bake_meshes = True. It computes exactly what the
import would materialise and refuses above 24 GB, naming the triangles, the gigabytes and
the fix. Verified against the real sources:
Guidemen, bake=True -> REFUSED
Crash 2 — Nanite assertion, 2026-09-15 02:37
Assertion failed: Nanite::IsSupportedBlendMode(ShadingMaterial)
NaniteShading.cpp Line 637 · 3 fatal hits
Nanite cannot render a material whose blend mode or shading model it does not support,
and the engine asserts rather than degrading. Nanite accepts Opaque and Masked, with
Default Lit or Unlit. Translucent and Additive assert.
Not yet fixed — the audit is written and waiting
Scripts/AuditNaniteMaterialCompatibility.py scans every landmark material for a Nanite
flag with an unsupported blend or shading mode. It needs the editor, which is closed.
Crash 3 — not a crash
Ensure condition failed: ParentNode
SimpleConstructionScript.cpp Line 960 · 2026-09-16
A handled ensure — logged as an error but the editor survives. It came from
SubobjectDataSubsystem.DeleteSubobject
The crash reader now separates handled ensures from fatal errors, so a benign ensure no
longer masquerades as a crash.
Scripts/ReadEditorCrashLog.py
One step instead of grepping: scans every log, classifies, prints the context and the fix.
Machine headroom — the underlying limit
physical RAM 63.77 GB (46.5 GB available)
page file 34.00 GB
commit limit 97.77 GB (72.5 GB available)
C: free space 59 GB of 1.9 TB (97% full)
The page file cannot grow into 59 GB of free space on a nearly full volume, which is why
the failure message was about the paging file rather than RAM. A 148 GB bake was never
What to do before the next import
1. Run python Scripts/ImportPreflight.py and read the verdict table.
2. If it says BAKE-FORBIDDEN, keep bake_meshes = False — the guards now
enforce this automatically and refuse the import otherwise.
3. Start from a freshly opened editor with nothing else heavy running.
4. Free space on C: so the page file can grow if it needs to.
5. After any crash, python Scripts/ReadEditorCrashLog.py.
Status
Fixed and verified: the out-of-memory class. The preflight tool runs and produces the risk table; all six bake-on-import scripts carry a guard that compiles and provably refuses the
Guidemen case (bake=True → refused, bake=False → allowed at 0.01 GB) while permitting legitimate large imports (the Wuxianmen winding variant at 11.01 GB).
Scripted but not yet run: the Nanite blend-mode audit. The editor is closed. That class is a real, reproduced fatal assertion from 2026-09-15 and remains unfixed until the audit runs.
Reported, needs your decision: C: is 97% full with 59 GB free, which is why the page file could not expand. That is a system-level fix, not something I should change for you.
Not addressed: crash-avoidance for the GPU path, and any crash occurring inside a plugin or a third-party tool. Only the two classes present in the logs were handled.
